scope: Conservative osmotic water exchange coupled to the passive resolved_tissue@1 ionic field model. Closed finite cells and exterior compartments, fixed membrane areas/capacitances/topology, explicit impermeant osmolyte particle counts and linear elastic pressures. Complete 16-field trajectories use one cell and one exterior owner for 2 ms at 310 K; separate multi-edge/multicell stages check shared owners. This is a Cells compliant-volume extension, not native BETSE volume-trajectory parity or a biological calibration.
checks: Compare pressure, flow, energy and conservative graph derivatives with an independent 80-digit Decimal oracle across osmotic, mechanical, mixed, zero-solute and shared-owner graphs, reversed edges and padding. Check common pressure offsets, sealed interfaces, nonnegative dissipation and the fixed-solute water-volume Jacobian bound. The bound is not a full coupled stability or accuracy guarantee.

Compare complete 16-field coupled derivatives and resolved potentials with independent scalar ionic and water equations at changed volumes, compact/padded layouts and reordered species. Every ionic stage uses current amount/current volume. Sealing water reduces exactly to the prior 12-field model. Explicit impermeant particle amounts are not inferred from fixed charge.

Five complete compiled 2-ms trajectories cover coupled swelling, sealed water, water-only dilution, shrinkage and independent off-grid ionic/water release schedules. Save complete histories and observations before assertions. Compare every field and potential against a segmented DOP853 reference; water alone changes no ionic amount or charge. These are numerical cases, not independent biological observations.

Keep existing ion, charge, capacitor and physical-energy tolerances. Add local/global volume-transfer identities, monotone water heat and the stable mixing/elastic energy correction using current ion amounts. Invalid bounded-volume trials and water controls reject without clipping, preserving all 16 fields. Fourfold reference tightening and three compiled RK4 grids test coupled accuracy independently of the step bound.

Require bitwise complete disk/fresh-process/terminal replay, an independently changed future water control, changed integration windows, full state/layout/clocks and a fresh ordinary CLI resume. Save actual arrays before comparisons. Run replay phases sequentially under the same process-tree resource guard.

Compare scalar worlds, combined/reversed worlds and separate one-world partitions, then resume worlds with different clocks including a terminal world. Retain stable world identities in offline 1-16 GPU and 1-4 Jupiter-node plans. Planning and L4 execution do not establish remote execution or a single tissue spanning devices.

Compare every saved CPU/L4 history and observation using unchanged unit-specific backend tolerances. GPU adaptive references must match normalized CPU inputs and refinement settings. Required reports and all evidence hashes are bound to the frozen source; failed evidence remains retained.

Use fresh bounded workers, the deterministic GPU policy, disabled persistent compilation cache and the recorded host allocator. Keep 4-GiB charged process-tree and individual RSS limits with an 8-GiB host reserve. Record GPU-busy and SM-active including host/compilation intervals. No automatic retry or follow-up.
scope_exclusions: Fixed areas, capacitances and topology with changing compliant volumes. No shape mechanics, solvent drag, extracellular fluid velocity field, junction water transport, cutting or remeshing.
Passive shared ionic/water model only. Integration with kinetic channels, pumps, calcium/ER, injury, assembly, finite metabolism and autonomous repair requires further models and qualification.

Native BETSE pressure/zero-hydrostatic-pressure flow snapshots were checked separately. Its pinned volume/concentration update block is inactive; no native evolving-volume trajectory claim. No wetlab fit or experimental validation.
Offline independent-world planning and local CPU/L4 execution only. No GH200/Jupiter qualification or single-tissue domain decomposition.
